title: Advancing Positron Imaging with Alginate-Based Tracers: Design, Synthesis, and Radiolabelling Methods☆
author: Bruno, Baiocco, et al.

steps.title: Prepare Sodium Alginate Solution
steps.instruction: Weigh the required amount of sodium alginate powder and distilled water to obtain the desired NaAlg concentration (typically 0.5‑4 wt % for low MGR or 2‑6 wt % for high MGR, with MGR 0.5‑1.6). Slowly add the powder to the water while stirring on a hot plate with a magnetic stirrer. Dissolve for 1‑2 h at 50‑80 °C (adjust time‑temperature according to supplier recommendations). Sonicate the solution at 20‑50 kHz for 10‑30 min or until no visible air bubbles remain.

steps.title: Prepare Metal Chloride Gelling Solution
steps.instruction: Weigh the appropriate amount of inorganic chloride salt (account for crystal hydration) and distilled water to achieve at least double the NaAlg concentration or ≥0.1 M. Add the salt to water at room temperature and stir with a magnetic stirrer until fully dissolved (5‑10 min). Use a multivalent cation (valence ≥+2, preferably ≥+3) to ensure alginate gelation.

steps.title: Set Up Extrusion Dripping Apparatus
steps.instruction: Load solution 1 into a syringe with a luer‑lock tip, attach a PTFE tube and extrusion‑dripping nozzle, and seal fittings with parafilm. Place the beaker containing solution 2 on a magnetic stirrer beneath a support stand. Clamp the nozzle so its tip is at the desired height above the surface of solution 2 and position the syringe pump adjacent to the stand.

steps.title: Flush Tubing and Prime System
steps.instruction: Temporarily remove the beaker of solution 2. Start the syringe pump at a slightly higher flow rate than the final set point and run for 30‑60 s to flush impurities from the tubing. Note the deposition area on the stirrer plate.

steps.title: Extrude Alginate Beads into Gelling Bath
steps.instruction: Reduce the flow rate to the selected value. Return the beaker of solution 2 beneath the nozzle, positioning it so droplets fall slightly off‑centre from the beaker middle, away from the stirrer vortex. Maintain stirring at approximately 500‑550 rpm. Continue extrusion until the desired number of beads is obtained or the syringe is empty.

steps.title: Gelation, Rinse, and Store Beads
steps.instruction: Allow the hydrogel beads to mature in the gelling solution under refrigerated conditions for the required gelation time. Separate beads with an appropriately sized mesh screen, rinse thoroughly with distilled water, and store the washed beads in distilled water under refrigerated conditions until further use.

steps.title: Configure Imaging Detector System
steps.instruction: Select the appropriate detector system for the planned imaging experiment (considering optimal tracer activity, field of view, and imaging quality). Position the equipment within the detector’s field of view so all regions of interest are captured. Fill the system with the required volume of non‑radioactive process media to enable immediate initiation after tracer introduction.

steps.title: Select Radiolabelling Method and Parameters
steps.instruction: Choose the tracer formulation and either the low‑temperature or evaporative radiolabelling method to be validated. Determine the radiolabelling parameters (e.g., initial water activity, radiolabelling time, number of beads, and expected radiochemical yield) required to achieve the optimal tracer activity for the selected detector system.

steps.title: Radiolabel Tracer Particles
steps.instruction: Perform radiolabelling of the alginate beads using the selected method (low‑temperature adsorption or evaporative adsorption) according to the parameters defined in the previous step.

steps.title: Prepare Control Tracer for Comparison
steps.instruction: Prepare a conventional tracer (e.g., ion‑exchange resin particles) in parallel and radiolabel it using the same method to provide a baseline for comparison with the alginate tracer.
